title: A Gemini Outage Blanked Out Two Video Segments | vitalii.no
description:
How a single-provider outage silently stripped AI direction from part of a daily video digest, and why the fix was a second backend, not a retry.

On October 7th, Gemini returned an error while my video-processor was asking it for visual direction on two digest segments. The GitHub Actions video pipeline (scripts/video-processor/llm-helper.js, visual-director.js) had exactly one LLM backend with no fallback, unlike the Edge Function side of the stack, which already had one. Those two segments rendered with no AI-generated direction at all, and nothing flagged it.

The fix adds Groq's free tier as a second backend in llm-helper.js, wired into visual-director.js and the three GitHub Actions workflow files that run it (custom-video.yml, daily-news-video.yml, process-video.yml). When the primary Gemini call fails now, the helper retries against Groq instead of returning nothing, so a segment still gets AI-planned visual direction.

The pipeline's LLM calls for visual direction now survive a single-provider outage instead of silently losing a segment's direction — closing the exact gap that caused the October 7th incident.
